subject: Private deployment identity validation + onboarding runbook questions
messages:
From: Priya Singh <psingh@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment identity mapping and SCIM expectations

Marcus / Rishi —

Thanks for taking the call last week. As we prep for the private control plane deployment inside our VPC, the security team asked for a short written summary of how Redwood intends to integrate with our identity stack. High-level constraints from our side:

- We will provide a SAML 2.0 IdP (Okta) for SSO.
- We need group-to-role mapping so that our AD groups map to specific Redwood roles (example: Acme PrivAdmins -> priv-admin; Acme DataOps -> priv-operator).
- SCIM push provisioning is preferred but we need to understand the delta vs full sync behavior and SCIM attributes you consume.
- Audit/logging: we need proof that control-plane admin actions are traceable to our SAML identities (userID or email) and retained for 365 days for SOC2 compliance.

Can you confirm:
1) The SAML attribute name(s) Redwood expects for role/group mapping (e.g. 'redwood:roles' or 'memberOf')?
2) Whether SCIM supports nested group imports and how role assignment occurs on first-login vs provisioning-only.
3) Any recommended session duration / assertion lifetime for SAML to avoid long-lived sessions in the private control plane.

Also attaching our IdP metadata will speed the test — I can share that once we lock a test window. We are aiming for a staging test between May 17–19 (PST).

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Head, Security Engineering
Acme Health

--
Attachment: acme-idp-metadata.xml (referenced, sent separately via secure transfer)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment identity mapping and SCIM expectations

Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, longer operational notes below and I attached a runbook + VPC diagram for your infra team.

Quick responses:
- SAML attribute: primary mapping uses 'redwood_roles' (multi-valued). We also accept 'memberOf' and can map Okta group DNs at setup time.
- SCIM: Redwood supports SCIM 2.0 push provisioning (create/update/replace/delete). We handle groups as first-class SCIM resources; nested groups are flattened at provisioning time and mapped according to the runbook rules.
- Session/assertion: we recommend assertion lifetime <= 5 minutes and session duration 1 hour for interactive admin sessions. For automation/service accounts we use short-lived tokens (15 min) minted by our platform with rotation.

Operational notes / runbook highlights (high-level):
1) Provisioning flow: IdP -> SCIM push -> Redwood SCIM endpoint (TLS mutual optional) -> provisioning service account used to write members/roles.
2) Role mapping: At onboarding we create configurable mappings: Okta group -> Redwood role. You can choose 'provision-only' or 'allow-SSO-assign' modes.
3) Service accounts: recommend creating a dedicated SCIM service account in Okta with only group read and member read privileges.
4) Audit: every control-plane action is logged with the asserted SAML subject and the SCIM provisioning audit shows deltas. Logs are exported to your SIEM via our syslog/CloudWatch forwarder.

Attachments included: redwood-privcp-iam-runbook-v1.2.pdf (runbook), diagram-vpc-iam.svg (network flow), acme-scim-example-mapping.csv (example mapping file).

Next steps:
- If May 17–19 works, suggest a 60-min window on May 18 09:00–10:00 PT to do an end-to-end SSO + SCIM test in our staging tenant. Please share IdP metadata and a couple of test users (one admin, one operator).

If useful, I can draft a minimal HubSpot/Confluence checklist for your SSO/SYNC team.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment identity mapping and SCIM expectations

Priya / Marcus —

A few security-specific points I want to call out before the test to avoid surprises:

- Audience restrictions: ensure the SAML assertion Audience includes the control-plane entity URL we provide during staging. We enforce audience_match by default.
- Attribute names: Marcus mentioned 'redwood_roles' — please ask Okta to include a multi-valued attribute with that name (or map an existing group claim to it). We prefer group claims over email-based role inference.
- Assertion lifetime / replay protection: keep assertion validity short (<=5m) and ensure your IdP signs assertions with SHA-256.
- SCIM auth: we support Bearer token and mTLS for SCIM endpoints. If you select mTLS, we'll provide cert fingerprint expectations; tokens should be rotated no less frequently than 90 days, ideally 30.
- Audit & retention: to be SOC2-compliant you asked for 365d logs; we can support that but will need to enable extended audit retention (this is an add-on for Private customers). I'll flag billing/contracting if you want us to enable retention at no extra cost during onboarding.

Also: we have a known tricky case where Okta sends nested group objects; our SCIM service will flatten but if you rely on nested semantics we need to document override rules in the mapping CSV. Please review the attached example mapping and flag any group names that should be treated specially.

—Rishi
Head of Security Integrations
Redwood Inference
